claims.text: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on the face of the record: the artifacts describe the same trip. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-00114; the gps_trace's first fix at 2026-08-07T18:40:00+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at exactly; its last fix at 19:20:00 matches trip_record.ended_at; and the fare_breakdown's charged_at of 19:20:24 sits 24 seconds clear of the recorded end of movement. Nothing on the identity limb is contested by either party.

The excess is established under POL-RD-01, measured from the figure that clause makes governing. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip_record's rounded copy may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace measures 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: the excess is far above the 20% of optimal gate and far above the 0.8 km absolute gate, so the finding does not depend on the rounded 24.0 km convenience figure (which would show 6.0 km and 33.3% on its own). The 18.0 km optimal is the platform's own route estimate, sourced to routing-engine-v3.2 on an 18:36 traffic snapshot.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no independent corroboration is required. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m between fixes, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace carries 241 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) are all disengaged, POL-RD-07(ii)'s corroboration rule does not bite, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route cannot open.

No clause exonerates this deviation, because the only candidate clause has nothing to run on. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that (a) names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, (b) has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and (c) supplies a shortest_lawful_alternative_km for the 130% cap formula. The only advisory artifact in the case, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING: weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, and its own detail records that no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. I cite that absence, not any contents — a missing artifact's absence is itself citable. The driver's congestion account, in his statement and in his chat reply ('AYE jam boss, this way faster'), names no advisory and cites no evidence ID, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. His account concedes the route was changed and disputes only the justification — the part he cannot evidence.

The driver's justification fails on the record's own timings, not merely on the missing advisory. The trip_record shows actual_duration_min of 40.0 against optimal_duration_min of 30.0 for the PIE westbound via Kim Keat Link optimal, so the route actually driven cost ten minutes more than the route the platform had selected for this trip at 18:36 — the opposite of 'this way faster'. A route that is 5.97 km longer and ten minutes slower on the platform's own measurements is not vindicated by the clock, and with no advisory to test, POL-RD-03's exoneration is unavailable and no adjusted optimal can be derived.

The detour was not rider-requested, so no part of the excess is excludable under POL-RD-04. That clause requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within three minutes after, identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, with corroboration run on chat_message.waypoint_hint rather than by geocoding a place name. The chat log holds exactly two messages: the rider's 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' and the driver's 'AYE jam boss, this way faster'. The rider's message is an objection to being taken up Adam Road, not a request for it, and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so no instruction exists and no 200 m waypoint test can be met.

The baseline is the booked optimal, because nothing was relocated. POL-RD-05 re-bases POL-RD-01 only where a pickup or dropoff point was amended after booking. On this trip pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. The booked endpoints — Bugis Junction, 200 Victoria St to Jurong East MRT (Exit B), 10 Jurong Gateway Rd — and the 18.0 km / 30 minute optimal therefore stand unamended and no substitute re-quote is available or permissible.

This is a solo trip, so POL-RD-12 cannot inflate the baseline and the rider is not being measured against any pooled itinerary. The pooled clause applies only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; here it is RYDE_X, solo_optimal_distance_km is null, and no distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider appears anywhere in the trace or the fare_breakdown. The 18.0 km figure the excess is measured against is the platform's matched figure for this trip.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it comes to SGD 13.70 on a PARTIAL_REFUND. Under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km optimal + 0.28 x 30.0 min optimal) x the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + ERP for gantries lying on the optimal route. Reading the multiplier from the fare_breakdown, as the clause expressly requires, gives 1.6: (3.80 + 13.50 + 8.40) x 1.6 = 41.12, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 2.50 for the Kim Keat Link gantry — the only gantry on the optimal route — for a recomputed_fare of 44.42. Refund = charged_total 58.10 - recomputed_fare 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 23.5% of charged_total, well below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to FULL_REFUND. The rider does not contest the 1.6 surge; it is applied to the recomputed optimal fare exactly as the clause directs, which is why the refund is a partial and not the whole distance difference. The rider is the filing party, so under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND returns this sum to him.

The second gantry the rider paid for was not on his route, and it is already inside the refund figure rather than additional to it. The fare_breakdown items two ERP lines totalling 4.50: PIE (Kim Keat Link towards Tuas) at 2.50, flagged on_optimal_route true, and PIE (Adam Rd towards Tuas) at 2.00, flagged on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(1), off-route ERP is ALREADY COMPREHENDED in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare of 44.42 includes only the on-optimal-route gantry. The 2.00 should be itemised separately in the ruling for transparency but must never be added on top of the 13.70. The rider seeks the single, non-duplicated figure and does not ask for the 2.00 twice.

This is not a phantom-gantry case, and no billing-integrity correction arises — but both crossings confirm the corridor actually driven. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of the gantry coordinates as a crossing. Both billed gantries are matched: the Kim Keat Link gantry has a nearest fix at 0.0 m at 18:55:30 and the Adam Road gantry at 8.76 m at 19:05:20, so both are real crossings rather than unmatched lines, POL-RD-10(8) does not fire, and no POL-RD-09(4) correction is claimed. The Adam Road crossing independently confirms the vehicle was on the PIE past Adam Road, exactly as the rider describes and as the driver's own chat reply acknowledges.

No corroboration gate applies to this rider, and no profile field is used against anyone beyond the tests that name them. POL-RD-08 imposes an extra corroboration requirement only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. This rider's figures are 1 and 1 respectively, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so the claim stands on the trace without any further source. These are the only rider fields cited, and they are cited only for the POL-RD-08 test, as POL-GEN-01 requires; lifetime counters, rating and account age are not relied on anywhere in this brief.

The record is complete enough to rule on, and it should be decided rather than escalated. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact; identity, trace distance and the fare lines are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so nothing drags confidence below the 0.70 floor and POL-RD-10(1) does not fire. Nor do the other triggers: trip identifiers match across the three core artifacts (limb 2); the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (limb 3); the timestamps are consistent with no backwards run and no drift beyond seconds (limb 4); the refund of 13.70 is under SGD 150.00 and under charged_total (limb 6); and no admissible evidence of comparable strength contradicts the rider (limb 7). As to limb 5, the missing advisory is deployed against the party asserting the congestion excuse and grounds no fact about this trip, so no ruling is built on an absent artifact. For completeness I disclose the only artifact below weight 1.0 in this brief: EV-ADVIS-00114-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, cited solely for its absence, which is the use the citation rules expressly permit.

The rider does not overreach on the remedy. The excess of 5.97 km and 33.17% clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate but is below both MATERIAL thresholds — 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute — so the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available, whether or not a pattern could be shown on the driver's figures (1 flag in 90 days over 412 completed trips). This is candidly a partial-refund case: the rider asks for the arithmetic SGD 13.70 under POL-RD-02 on a charged_total of SGD 58.10, not for the whole SGD 15.00 contested and not for any round-number award.

claims.text: The deviation on this trip is established but NOT material, and that caps everything that follows. The governing measurement is the trace rather than the rounded copy of it: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km, an excess of 5.97 km and 33.17%. That passes both POL-RD-01 establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20%, so the rider is right that a deviation exists and I do not pretend otherwise. But it fails both materiality gates: 5.97 km is under the 8.0 km figure and 33.17% is under the 50% figure. The consequence is that no POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is required, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no conduct referral arises on this trip.

Concession, and it is a real one: the driver does not discharge the POL-RD-08 burden. His own counterparty statement says 'No advisory that I know of'; the chat log contains only 'AYE jam boss, this way faster', with waypoint_hint null on both messages; and the single traffic-advisory artifact on the case, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I disclose that impairment rather than dress it up. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory naming a road, a validity window and a matched deviation around the affected segment; with no advisory at all, limbs (a) to (c) cannot be run and no exoneration attaches to the driver's route choice.

The one excusable explanation the driver offers is the one the record cannot test, and that matters for the disposition. The driver asserts the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit, and the artifact that would have decided that assertion — EV-ADVIS-00114-01 — is MISSING with weight 0.0 and carries a BLOCKING issue detail recording that no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. POL-RD-10(5) names precisely this situation, 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory', and directs escalation rather than a monetary ruling. On that reading the exoneration question is undecidable on this record, the case goes to a human with the disputed amount held rather than refunded, and I ask the chamber to prefer that route over a confident ruling on an incomplete record.

If the chamber rules on the money, the surge must be carried at the figure the artifact records, not at zero. POL-RD-02 requires the multiplier to be read from the fare_breakdown, where it is 1.6, and applied to the whole optimal base of 25.70 (3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 = 13.50 distance + 0.28 x 30.0 = 8.40 time). That adds 15.42 of surge uplift to the recomputed fare and takes the same 15.42 off the refund. A recomputation that quietly dropped the surge would refund the rider for a surge he expressly told the platform he accepts.

The remedy is arithmetic and it is well below both the rider's demand and the charge. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-route ERP = 44.42, against a charged_total of 58.10. The refund is therefore 13.68, payable 13.70 once rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 under POL-RD-02 — not the 15.00 the rider contests and nowhere near the 58.10 full refund. The refund is 23.5% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND, and it is above the 0.50 de minimis floor so the rider does take something. The 1.30 by which the rider's figure exceeds the arithmetic corresponds to no line of the fare_breakdown, and POL-RD-02 does not permit a discretionary top-up to a round number.

The rider's $4.50 ERP complaint is wrong by half and is in any event already paid for by the refund above. Of the two charged lines, only the Adam Road gantry at $2.00 is off the optimal route; the Kim Keat Link gantry at $2.50 is on the optimal route, and the driver's trace passes it at a nearest fix of 0.0 m. The POL-RD-02 recomputation therefore carries the 2.50 inside the recomputed fare and leaves the 2.00 out, which means the off-route ERP is already comprehended in the 13.68 refund. Under POL-RD-09(1) that line is itemised for transparency but must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, so the rider recovers the off-route gantry once and not twice.

There is no billing-integrity defect here and no standalone correction is due. Both billed gantries are matched to the trace well inside the 250 m crossing radius that POL-RD-09(4) uses — Kim Keat Link at a nearest fix of 0.0 m and Adam Road at 8.76 m — so neither is a phantom line and no line is refundable under that limb. Nor is the trace impaired for policy purposes: coverage is 100% over 241 fixes at a 10 second interval, with no gaps, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so POL-RD-07 does not bite and the excess stands on the trace alone without need of independent corroboration.

POL-RD-06 stays shut on this trip's own numbers. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the three-flag trigger the clause sets, and 1 flag over driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 412 is a ratio of about 0.0024, far below the 0.05 ratio the clause requires with at least 40 completed trips. Neither limb of the pattern test is met, and the deviation is not material in any event. No repeat-pattern finding, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) can be built on this profile — and POL-GEN-01 forbids using any other field on the profile, such as the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, to do the work this test cannot.

To both parties: this is my ruling on trip TRP-00114 (Friday 7 August 2026, Bugis Junction to Jurong East MRT).

The deviation is established. The trace (EV-GPS-00114) measures 23.97 km against the platform's booked optimal of 18.0 km (EV-TRIP-00114) — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.2%. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal), so a partial refund is due. It does NOT reach either MATERIAL gate (more than 50%, or more than 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 driver-conduct check, no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral arise.

The driver's explanation does not excuse the deviation. POL-RD-03 exonerates a detour only where a traffic_advisory names a corridor the optimal route uses and covers the time the vehicle would have been there. There is no such advisory: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), and the record shows no advisory covering the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36–19:20 window; the driver himself states he knew of none. His congestion account also cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not discharge the burden. The excess is established under POL-RD-01, measured from the figure that clause makes governing. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no independent corroboration is required. No clause exonerates this deviation, because the only candidate clause has nothing to run on. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that (a) names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, (b) has a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and (c) supplies a shortest_lawful_alternative_km for the 130% cap formula.
